credentials.description: Simple demo root login. R-SUPER in both realms; wildcard access, everything visible everywhere. Same credentials on every dashboard and stable across a profile switch.
Super-user. Wildcard access; everything visible everywhere.
System administrator. Manages users, roles, IdPs; DENIED on every analytic mart read.
Security officer. Read-only on audit + observability; approves privileged actions (break-glass).
National-scope decision-maker. Every region, every programme; aggregate / deidentified data only.
Same widgets as R-DEC but region filter constrained to Oromia.
Internal analyst. SQL Lab access; saved queries; reads every cataloged mart.
Workshop access; submits artifacts; production marts DENIED (workshop sandbox only).
Metadata + lineage + DSA workflow. Data plane intentionally denied.
Unauthenticated public visitor. Public landing + catalogue + articles. No PHI.

scenarios.title: Sign in as every demo role and watch the dashboard adapt
steps: Open the public dashboard at https://public.127.0.0.1.nip.io/ as an anonymous visitor (no sign-in). Note the public widgets only.
Click 'Sign in' in the top-right; the chooser opens. Pick 'Internal BI' and complete PKCE as dec.nat. Observe the full national-scope BI dashboard.
Sign out, sign back in as kebede.oromia. The same Internal BI dashboard now shows the Region filter pre-set to Oromia and disabled.
Sign out, sign in as solomon.m to the admin dashboard. The Roles + Users + SSO sections render. Navigate to Internal BI - you get a 'no dashboard access' page.
Sign in as sci.demo to workshop. The Workspace + Groups + Artifacts sections render. Try to read a production mart through the API - see the deny-mart-direct-api scenario.
scenarios.expected_result: Each role sees a strictly different surface. Same code paths; different decisions.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The four axes are the entire UI-shape story. Same React app, five different surfaces from the same code, driven only by role_dashboard / role_widget / role_global_filter.

scenarios.title: Citizen Fayda-verifies on an access request
steps: Open the public dashboard at https://public.127.0.0.1.nip.io/ and click Request access.
On the modal, click Verify with Fayda. A popup opens to Fayda Replica at http://localhost:8096/.
Pick any citizen (e.g. Almaz Hailu) and click Sign in.
The popup closes; the form is pre-filled with name + Fayda ID; a green Fayda-verified badge appears.
Complete the form (purpose, dashboards requested) and submit.
Sign in to admin as solomon.m, open Access Requests, see the new request with a Fayda-verified pill.
One-click approve - user created in Keycloak with verified_via=fayda + user_linked_identity row.
scenarios.expected_result: End-to-end Fayda federation handshake working against the mock; admin sees + approves the verified request.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Government-scale identity. Same SPA flow against the real Fayda endpoint just swaps a URL.

scenarios.title: Single sign-on across all five dashboards
steps: Sign in as root to the demo dashboard (http://localhost:8500/).
Open a new tab to admin (8086). Sign-in chip says 'root, R-SUPER' - no second login.
Open BI (8087). Same chip. Same for workshop (8085).
Open public (8088). Top-right says 'Hi, root (R-SUPER)' instead of 'Sign in'.
scenarios.expected_result: One sign-in propagates to every dashboard via Keycloak silent-SSO.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Bearer SSO via Keycloak gives the same UX as cookie SSO without the cross-origin headaches.

scenarios.title: Sign in via Google (social federation)
prerequisites: Google IdP brokered into the moh-staff realm
steps: Open public dashboard and click Sign in.
Pick the federated-SSO tab and click Continue with Google.
Complete Google's OAuth flow.
Land back at NHDW with a user_linked_identity row of kind=google.
scenarios.expected_result: Same authenticated-user surface as any other login path.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Same model supports social logins for low-trust surfaces.

scenarios.title: Onboard EHIA via SAML federation at runtime
steps: Sign in to admin as solomon.m. Navigate to SSO.
Click + New IdP, choose SAML 2.0.
Paste the EHIA mock's metadata URL and save.
Backend mirrors metadata to ops_identity.identity_source AND calls Keycloak Admin API to register the alias.
Open public dashboard's Sign in; the IdP picker now lists EHIA.
Complete SAML login - auto-provisioned in Keycloak + linked identity recorded.
scenarios.expected_result: New IdP wired end-to-end in under 60 seconds, without restart.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Federation onboarding as an admin-UI form instead of a service ticket.

scenarios.title: Create a new role end-to-end (R-RHB-AMHARA)
steps: Sign in as root to admin. Navigate to Roles and click + New role.
Code R-RHB-AMHARA, name RHB Director Amhara, combine_strategy=union.
Save. The 4-axis grant editor opens.
Axis A (dashboards): check internal-bi + public.
Axis B (global filters): for internal-bi/disease, set the region filter to [Amhara].
Axis C (widgets): on internal-bi/disease, select the same widgets R-DEC has.
Save. New policy_revision row written; YAML round-trips via dump_seed.py.
Create a new user kebede.amhara and assign R-RHB-AMHARA.
Sign in as that user, open BI - Region filter shows Amhara only, maps + KPIs filtered.
scenarios.expected_result: The new role behaves identically to R-RHB-OROMIA but scoped to Amhara. Zero code change.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Adding a regional director used to require code + redeploy. Now it's an admin-UI form.

scenarios.title: Edit a role's widget grants and see the dashboard adapt
steps: Two browser tabs. Tab 1: admin as root. Tab 2: BI as dec.nat.
In tab 2, observe the Disease page - dz-outbreaks-table widget visible.
In tab 1, Roles, R-DEC, Widgets, internal-bi/disease, uncheck dz-outbreaks-table, save.
In tab 2, reload. The widget is gone. audit_silent_deny row written.
Back in tab 1, re-check the widget and save.
Tab 2 reload - widget is back.
scenarios.expected_result: Permission changes propagate to a new dashboard render immediately, audited both ways.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Live permission management is rare; usually it's edit-YAML + redeploy + wait 20 min.

scenarios.title: Filter-scope cascade - narrow Oromia user can't widen
steps: Sign in as kebede.oromia to BI.
On the Disease page, the Region filter shows Oromia only and is disabled.
In the URL bar, manually append ?region=Tigray. The page rejects the param.
Open dev tools, rewrite a mart fetch to include region=Tigray. Send.
Gateway returns 403: filter values not allowed for your role: region=Tigray.
scenarios.expected_result: Filter scope enforced at both UI render time AND data fetch time.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Defense in depth. UI-only enforcement is trivially bypassed; gateway-side intersection at fetch is the real story.

scenarios.title: Audit trail for every permission change
steps: Generate some audit rows by performing role edits in a separate window.
Sign in as sec.officer to admin, open Audit.
Chronological list of audit_permission_change rows - who, when, what diff.
Click a row to see the before/after JSON diff.
Filter by user, date, table, op.
scenarios.expected_result: Every write is captured with before/after, attributed to a user.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Auditors require change-attribution; this is the canonical evidence.

scenarios.title: OPA decides a mart read - allow + deny live
steps: On the demo control room, trigger R-DEC reads HIV cascade aggregate - 200 OK + rows.
Trigger R-OPS-ADM reads HIV cascade - 403 with reason R-OPS-ADM data-plane deny-all (intentional).
Trigger R-PUB-ANON reads AEFI lineage - 403 with reason from R-PUB-ANON rego.
Trigger OPA decide direct - inspect the raw OPA decision payload.
scenarios.expected_result: Same gateway, same endpoint, opposite verdicts - purely from the role.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Concretises the role-to-OPA chain. Auditors trust what they can poke at.

scenarios.title: Edit a role's rego policy and see the verdict flip
steps: On the demo control room, trigger R-DEC reading HIV cascade - 200 OK.
On the host, edit shared_resource/roles/r-dec.yaml and remove the PRG/aggregate permission.
Run python3 7_security/opa/scripts/compile.py and docker restart opa.
Re-trigger the same scenario - 403 with the rego deny reason.
Restore the perm, recompile, restart. Trigger again - 200.
scenarios.expected_result: Mart-level enforcement is a config artifact reviewers can edit.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Policy-as-code review and hot reload, central to defensible health data sharing.

scenarios.title: Catalog vs policy drift fails the gateway boot
steps: On the host, change bi_programme_hiv_cascade_total mart_attrs to subject=FAC.
Reseed the DB.
Restart the gateway.
The gateway exits with 'OPA self-test failed for N case(s) under OPA_ENFORCE=true; refusing to start.'
Revert the change, reseed, restart - boot succeeds.
scenarios.expected_result: Catalog/policy drift is a startup failure, not a silent prod incident.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Prevents the looks-like-its-gating-but-actually-allows-everything class of OPA bug.

scenarios.title: Issue a PAT and use it from a notebook
steps: Sign in as analyst.ana to admin, API Tokens, New token (my-notebook, 30 days, no scope override).
Save. The secret is shown ONCE - copy it. Format nhdw_pat_<prefix>_<48 chars>.
Open JupyterHub, new notebook.
Set NHDW_PAT env var, then call the gateway with Authorization: Bearer NHDW_PAT.
The mart returns rows. Same OPA + 4-axis chain that gates the SPA gates this notebook call.
scenarios.expected_result: Programmatic mart access works through the standard gateway, no separate API path.
scenarios.why_it_matters: One API for everything - the data-platform story in one demo.

scenarios.title: PAT scope narrows the owner's permissions
steps: Issue a PAT with scope=[programs=HIV] for analyst.ana (who has access to all programmes).
Use the PAT to read bi_programme_hiv_cascade_total with programme=HIV - success.
Use the PAT to read bi_programme_tb_cohort with programme=TB - 403, scope intersected to HIV.
Use analyst.ana's Bearer JWT directly - both reads succeed.
scenarios.expected_result: Token scope = owner perms intersection token override. Token can narrow, never widen.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Export-this-dataset-for-a-partner: issue a tightly-scoped token instead of full credentials.

scenarios.title: Revoke a PAT and see the next request 401
steps: With a PAT issued above, make a successful API call.
Sign in to admin as analyst.ana, API Tokens, revoke that PAT.
Retry the same API call - 401 PAT revoked.
View the PAT's audit trail - see the revocation row + every prior call.
scenarios.expected_result: Revocation is immediate; no token sits in a cache.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Incident response: leaked PAT is one click from inert.

scenarios.title: System integration via Keycloak service account
steps: In Keycloak admin, create a client nhdw-partner-pepfar, type confidential, service-accounts-enabled.
Assign the SA the role R-CONS-PRT.
Request a client_credentials token from Keycloak's token endpoint.
Use the token to call the gateway - the same JWT path the dashboards use.
scenarios.expected_result: Machine-to-machine via standard OAuth2 client_credentials; no separate API-key plumbing.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Identity-provider-managed credentials with automatic rotation.

scenarios.title: Role visits a dashboard it can't access
steps: Sign in as sci.demo. Land on workshop - works.
Navigate to https://admin.127.0.0.1.nip.io/ (admin). /auth/me reports the user; resolver returns no spec - no-access page.
Try https://internal-bi.127.0.0.1.nip.io/ (BI). Same - dashboard internal-bi not accessible to your role.
scenarios.expected_result: Wrong-dashboard navigation is gracefully denied with a clear message; no leak.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Denial UX is part of the security story. A generic 403 beats a stack trace.

scenarios.title: Direct API read of a mart you can't see
steps: On the demo control room, trigger R-PUB-ANON reads bi_safety_aefi_lineage.
Gateway returns 403 with reason from R-PUB-ANON rego.
View the audit pane - denial captured to ops_audit.gateway_query with policy_decision=deny.
scenarios.expected_result: Negative outcome is observable and auditable.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Did-anyone-try-to-read-this is a frequent auditor question; the denial trail answers it.

scenarios.title: Read of an uncataloged mart is refused
steps: Trigger an explicit read of marts.nonexistent_table as R-SUPER.
Gateway returns 403 - mart not cataloged - refusing to serve under OPA_ENFORCE=true.
Even R-SUPER can't read what isn't in mart_attrs.
scenarios.expected_result: Catalog membership is a prerequisite for service, regardless of role.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Even super-users can't accidentally serve a new mart before security review.

scenarios.title: Filter value outside the role's allowed set
steps: Sign in as kebede.oromia.
Use Dev Tools to inject region=Tigray into a widget data fetch.
Gateway returns 403: filter values not allowed for your role: region=Tigray.
scenarios.expected_result: UI hides the disallowed value AND the gateway rejects it at fetch.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Most common authz-bypass class: trust the client. NHDW doesn't.

scenarios.title: Expired PAT denial
steps: Issue a PAT with expires_in_days=1, wait for it to expire.
Try to use it - 401 PAT expired.
scenarios.expected_result: Time-bounded credentials; expiry enforced at every request.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Long-lived tokens are a compliance risk; NHDW PATs default 90-day expiry.

scenarios.title: Community group lifecycle - create, join, contribute
steps: Sign in as sci.demo to workshop, Groups, + New group.
Name WHO Africa Region Surveillance, visibility open.
As root, observe the new group in admin Groups (view_audit).
Back as sci.demo, submit an artifact (notebook) to the group.
As root (approve_artifact_promotion), promote the artifact from sandbox to community library.
scenarios.expected_result: End-to-end contribution path with audit at every step.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The community story isn't just open access; it's a governed contribution pipeline.

scenarios.title: Break-glass for raw-PHI access (two-person rule)
steps: As solomon.m, request break-glass for raw mart vault_business.enc_patient_visit.
System issues a pending approval; sec.officer is paged.
As sec.officer, sign in and approve.
solomon.m gets a 30-minute scoped token; session fully recorded.
After 30 min token auto-expires; audit trail shows request, approval, every query made.
scenarios.expected_result: Privileged access requires two operators, is time-bounded, fully audited.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Auditors specifically ask about break-glass; this lands trust.

scenarios.title: Silent denies surface in admin audit
steps: Have a role with no widget access try to navigate a dashboard.
Resolver writes a audit_silent_deny row.
As sec.officer, open admin Audit Silent denies. See the rows.
Click one to see kc_sub, widget hidden, reason.
scenarios.expected_result: User-couldn't-see-X investigations have a concrete trail.
scenarios.why_it_matters: 'Logged in but dashboard is blank' tickets usually need log archaeology; this is a one-page view.

scenarios.title: Open the chat panel as four different roles — see four different suggestion lists
steps: Sign in to Internal BI as dec.nat (R-DEC). Click the chat FAB bottom-right.
Note the intro suggestions — they're decision-maker prompts about programme outcomes.
Sign out, sign back in as analyst.ana (R-CONS-ANA). Open the chat. Suggestions are now SQL-leaning.
Repeat for kebede.oromia (R-RHB-OROMIA) — suggestions reference Oromia explicitly.
Repeat for sci.demo (R-CONS-SCI) — suggestions lean toward exploratory analysis.
scenarios.expected_result: The same chat panel boots from /api/chat/intro with a different per-role suggestion list. The catalogue is computed server-side from chat_configs/internal-bi/intents.yaml — no client logic.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Tool grants AND prompt suggestions are role-driven. Operators see what's relevant to THEM without the bot being told who they are at the prompt layer.

scenarios.title: Roles without bi-assistant don't see the chat FAB
steps: Sign in to Internal BI as shewaye.a (R-CONS-PRT, partner consumer).
Look at the bottom-right corner. There is NO chat FAB.
Open dev tools → Network. The page boots normally; the only chat-related request is /api/chat/intro which returns 403.
Sign in as dec.nat. The same dashboard, same code path — the FAB renders.
scenarios.expected_result: ChatbotPanel returns null when /api/chat/intro responds 403. No widget = no UI surface; the access decision is made server-side.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Permissions don't just hide DATA — they hide whole CAPABILITIES. The chatbot is a widget (placement=chrome.fab) granted at dashboard level; ungranted users see nothing.

scenarios.title: Ask the bot 'what's on this page?' — it reads the live DOM
steps: Sign in to Internal BI as dec.nat. Navigate to the Disease page.
Open the chat. Ask: 'What widgets are on this page right now?'
Watch the network tab. The bot calls window.__nhdwDashboard.read_page() via the gateway's tool-call protocol.
The answer enumerates the visible widget IDs (dz-kpi-strip, dz-region-map, dz-woreda-table, ...).
scenarios.expected_result: The bot's tool_call surfaces in the panel as a collapsible row. Clicking expands the JSON it received from read_page — including widget IDs, titles, and current global filter values.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Introspection means the bot doesn't HAVE to be told context — it asks the SPA. Same code on every page; no per-page wiring.

scenarios.title: Tell the bot 'show me Oromia outbreaks' — it navigates + filters
steps: Sign in as dec.nat (R-DEC has no region pin → full national scope).
From Overview, open the chat. Ask: 'Take me to disease surveillance and filter to Oromia.'
Watch the page: it switches to Disease, then the region filter sets to 'Oromia'.
Open the tool_calls drawer: you'll see navigate_to_page + apply_global_filter, both executed SPA-side.
scenarios.expected_result: Two SPA-executor tool calls in sequence. The bot's answer confirms the new context. The user could have done both clicks manually — the bot just did them faster.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The bot is an OPERATOR, not just a chatbot. It controls the UI within the user's own permission scope.

scenarios.title: Analyst asks the bot a data question — it runs SQL within their scope
steps: Sign in as analyst.ana (R-CONS-ANA — has run_sql in their chatbot-tools scope).
Open the chat. Ask: 'How many active outbreaks are there per region?'
The bot composes a SELECT against marts.bi_programme_outbreak_signals (within OPA scope) and runs it.
The collapsible tool_call shows the SQL it wrote AND the row response. The bot's answer paraphrases the data.
scenarios.expected_result: The gateway delegates run_sql through /api/sql/execute which is gated by per-table OPA + the user's role_widget_filter scope. Rows come back, the bot summarises them in natural language.
scenarios.why_it_matters: SQL is the bot's most powerful tool — and the riskiest. Per-table OPA + user-scope intersection ensures the bot can NEVER exceed what its user would see by running the same query in the SQL Lab.

scenarios.title: RHB director (no run_sql) asks for raw data — bot refuses without leaking schema
steps: Sign in as kebede.oromia (R-RHB-OROMIA — chatbot-tools scope is ['read', 'interact'], NO run_sql).
Open the chat. Ask: 'Show me the raw rows from marts.bi_programme_outbreak_signals.'
The bot's catalogue doesn't include run_sql. Its answer says it can't run SQL but offers to navigate to the outbreaks widget instead.
scenarios.expected_result: No tool_call → no leakage. The bot routes to its available tools (read_page, navigate_to_page) and doesn't reveal schemas, table names, or row counts the user couldn't otherwise see.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Defense in depth: the gateway never EXPOSES tools the user can't invoke. The model literally doesn't know run_sql exists for this user — it can't be tricked into using it.

scenarios.title: Same prompt, two roles — the bot's available tool catalogue is different
steps: Have two browser profiles open: one signed in as analyst.ana, one as kebede.oromia.
Ask both bots the same question: 'List the top 5 facilities by outbreak count.'
analyst.ana's bot uses run_sql against the production mart. Catalogue includes read + run_sql + interact.
kebede.oromia's bot navigates to the hotspot facilities table and points the user at the regional rows already filtered to Oromia. Catalogue = read + interact.
Inspect /api/chat/start responses — different `executor` paths, different tools per session.
scenarios.expected_result: Two sessions, two distinct tool catalogues, two answer strategies — driven entirely by the chatbot-tools widget_filter values on each role.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The bot's BEHAVIOUR — not just its data — is a function of authorisation. Different roles get different products without a product change.

scenarios.title: Open the panel network tab — see the round-trip protocol in action
steps: Sign in as analyst.ana. Open dev tools → Network → filter 'chat'.
Ask the bot something that needs multiple SPA tools: 'Go to the disease page and tell me which widgets I'm allowed to see.'
First request: POST /api/chat/start — returns a tool_call (kind: navigate_to_page).
SPA executes the tool; second request: POST /api/chat/continue with session_id + tool_result.
Returns another tool_call (kind: read_page) → continue again → finally an `answer`.
Each round respects MAX_ROUNDS=6 (gateway env). After 6 the bot is forced to answer with whatever it has.
scenarios.expected_result: Two or three rounds visible. Each round is a small token-spend. The local 3B model never holds the full context — only enough to pick the next action.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Progressive disclosure makes a tiny model usable. The session lives in-process for 5 minutes; no DB write, no privacy trail beyond the audit log.

scenarios.title: Continue endpoint refuses cross-user session re-use
steps: Sign in as analyst.ana. Ask a question that triggers a tool_call. Copy the session_id from the response in dev tools.
In a new private window, sign in as dec.nat.
POST /api/chat/continue with the OTHER user's session_id + any tool_result.
Gateway returns 403 'session belongs to a different user'.
scenarios.expected_result: Sessions are per-user. The continue endpoint validates session.user_kc_sub matches the caller's kc_sub. Stealing a session_id buys you nothing.
scenarios.why_it_matters: The session_id is convenience, not authn. Every continue still validates the Bearer against the same kc_sub that started the session.

scenarios.title: Bot hits MAX_ROUNDS=6 — gracefully stops with whatever answer it has
steps: Open the chat as dec.nat. Ask a deliberately broad question: 'Compare every region across every disease across every period.'
The bot starts running tools — read_page, possibly run_sql.
On the 7th attempt the gateway disables tools and forces an answer turn. The bot replies with a partial summary.
tool_calls drawer shows 6 rounds; the final answer mentions the budget cap.
scenarios.expected_result: Bounded latency + bounded spend per question. No runaway loops; no hung sessions.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Local LLMs are slow and easy to derail. The round budget is the load-bearing safety mechanism — it's why you can deploy a 3B model in front of users.

scenarios.title: Scale internal-bi from 1 to 3 replicas live and watch the cluster react
prerequisites: k3d cluster `nhdw` is up + gateway has the in-cluster ServiceAccount (gateway-rbac.yaml)
steps: Sign in to the admin dashboard as solomon.m (R-OPS-ADM).
Navigate to Infrastructure → Health & topology.
Click the Trigger button below to scale internal-bi to 3 replicas.
Run `kubectl -n nhdw get pods -l app=internal-bi -w` in a terminal — 2 new pods appear within seconds.
Click Trigger again with replicas=1 to scale back down; old pods terminate.
scenarios.expected_result: The K8s API accepts the scale patch; the deployment's replica count + ready-pod count both reflect the new value in <10s. The gateway's RoleBinding (apps/deployments/scale → patch) is what makes this work.
scenarios.why_it_matters: Live infrastructure operations are the heart of an admin console. The trigger uses the same gateway endpoint a future HPA + topology widget will consume — proves the K8s control path is wired end-to-end.
